notes: Both LLM and peer reviewers express uncertainty about PTEN protein levels (C102, C103). Both note the disconnect between 2-5 fold mRNA increase and only ~20% protein increase. Peer reviewers request Western blot validation and phosphorylation status of PTEN targets, while LLM acknowledges the need for additional protein-level validation.

Substantial disagreement on p38MAPK-mediated U6atac stabilization (C5, C27, C72, C74, C76, C77). LLM finds evidence strongly supported by anisomycin experiments and inhibitor studies. Peer reviewers request additional quantitation of U4atac/U6atac levels and di-snRNP formation, citing concerns about free U6atac excess, indicating they need more data before accepting the claims.

Disagreement on U6atac regulation of cytokine production through PTEN (C8, C31, C32, C96, C97, C99, C100, C101). LLM finds the regulatory role well-supported by complementary experiments. Peer reviewers express concern that cytokine effects may not be direct consequences of PTEN regulation, noting PTEN knockdown alone doesn't affect cytokine expression without anisomycin, and request direct PTEN protein measurements.

Partial overlap on U6atac dependence on Pol II and Pol III (C4, C76, C77). LLM finds this supported, but peer review R1 addresses broader concerns about U6atac stability and regulation that encompass only a subset of claims in LLM R2. Peer reviewers' request for U4atac/U6atac quantitation relates to the broader regulatory context.

Minimal overlap on U6atac short half-life (C3 only). LLM finds the half-life claim well-supported by multiple lines of evidence. Peer review R1 addresses broader U6atac stability and regulation issues (C3-C5, C27, C72, C74, C76, C77) with uncertainty, requesting additional quantitation data. The peer review concern is more comprehensive than the specific half-life claim.

LLM evaluates RNA-seq analysis of minor intron splicing efficiency variation (C45-C61) as supported. No corresponding peer review result addresses these specific claims about the wide variation in minor intron splicing efficiency.

LLM evaluates widespread transcriptome effects of U6atac inactivation (C62-C70) as supported. No corresponding peer review result directly addresses these claims about the 2088 down-regulated genes and alternative splicing events.

LLM evaluates p38MAPK-induced U6atac increase and enhanced minor intron splicing (C6, C28, C29, C82-C90) as supported. While peer review R2 addresses downstream cytokine effects, no peer review directly evaluates the connection between p38MAPK and minor intron splicing efficiency.

LLM evaluates the molecular switch hypothesis (C10, C33, C34, C107-C109, C128, C130, C131, C133, C134) as supported. No corresponding peer review result addresses this overarching mechanistic interpretation about minor introns functioning as U6atac-regulated switches.
LLM evaluates custom ncRNA microarray validation (C135-C139) as supported. No corresponding peer review result addresses these methodological validation claims.
LLM evaluates nascent transcript RNA-seq methodology (C140-C145) as supported. No corresponding peer review result addresses these methodological claims about the RNA-seq approach.

LLM evaluates U6atac as rate-limiting for ~200 minor intron-containing genes (C7, C24-C26, C50, C51) as supported. No corresponding peer review result addresses these specific claims about rate-limiting effects.
LLM evaluates luciferase reporter assays and cell-type generalizability (C78-C81) as supported. No corresponding peer review result addresses these validation experiments across multiple cell types.
